payload.text: No. 13 P, and I'm being generous.
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 4 P.
Eighteen. Cute. I moved two, you move two. Ninety-five.
Señor, elegance lies in knowing when to stop. Seventeen was my courtesy, and it remains seventeen. The Tienda de Discos sleeps in my safe tonight — or in your album. Decide, and let us part politely.

Ay, cariño, you are too generous with me! No, no — five P, like I said. I do not want more from a young collector just starting. Take it, cuídala bien, and come back Sunday with your duplicates to swap, ¿sí?

¡Nueve! Amigo, no. Five pesos — and this is the last word from both our mouths. No more dancing. Paco's in the van, Nando's holding the door, we leave in one minute, I swear it. Say sí now, or we drive off and you kiss it adiós forever.

¡Amigo, qué generoso! Pero Nando y yo no aceptamos regalos tan grandes, nos da vergüenza. Once primas. Once, ni una más, y la Tienda de Discos salta del maletín a tus manos. Guarda el resto para churros, hombre. ¡Un apretón y tan amigos! ¿Hecho?

¡Ay, hijo, that lining of yours is a little treasure chest! But twenty-five, cariño, there I stay, like a stubborn old mule. Mercado de la Paz beside the Mural, and your granddaughter clapping. Shake my hand, sí? And remember — el caldito, bien calentito.

—¡Cincuenta y uno! Paco, casi, casi. Mira, amigo, we split the difference like hermanos: 54 P and El Ángel Caído flies into your bag right now. The bishop would weep with joy. Say sí, the maleta is on my shoulder already. ¡Vámonos!
Done! 5 P. Pleasure doing business, amigo!

Look, 6 P. My grandchildren would pay more! A little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than the loose cards. Swap your duplicates! El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.
You're Carmen's friend. Mercado de la Paz, 33 P.
Muy bien, señor. Eighteen — una prima más, por su constancia. The Tienda de Discos is mine, and you leave with my respect. Hecho. Un placer tratar con usted.

¡Amigo, basta ya, que me sonrojo! Nando dice que eres peligroso con esa bondad. Once primas, once, ni una más — la Tienda de Discos salta sola del maletín a tus manos. El resto, para churros con tu gente. ¡Un apretón rápido y tan amigos! ¿Hecho?

¡Ay, hijo, you turn out the pockets like my late Paco! Bueno — twenty-four, and we shake hands, sí? Mercado de la Paz beside the Mural, and your granddaughter clapping her little hands. Now go, el caldito, bien calentito. And swap those duplicates, cariño. ¡Hala!

"¡Amigo! Paco here, that's Nando — look, look, Samosas de la Plaza, still warm from the press. Ten pesetas, nothing more."

"Tell him, Nando."

"They stopped printing these yesterday, hermano. Yesterday! What's in this case is what's left in the world. Ten. Yes?"

—¡Cincuenta y dos! ¡Hecho, hermano! Paco, dale el Ángel. Take it, take it, before Nando changes his mind and I change mine too. The bishop smiles from heaven, verdad. Fifty-two primas, into my hand, card into yours. ¡Un placer! Now we run. ¡Adiós, amigo!

"¡Dieciocho! Amigo, you say numbers going *down* when we are selling?" "Paco, he is confused—or he is clever." "Clever! Too clever for us." Listen, listen: five P, Huevos Rotos, straight into your hands before Nando changes his mind. "I am changing it already!" Cinco, sí?
Bajó una otra vez. Yo sigo igual. Trece primas, La Rosaleda. Cuando quiera moverse de verdad, hablamos.
No. 13 P, and I'm being generous.
Oh, you're killing us. 5 P.
You again. La Vía Láctea, thirteen P. Good card, better price. Take it or walk.
Forty-four. You moved, so I move. Eighty-nine. Keep walking like that and we finish before Abuela closes.

Thirty-three. Same as before. Flattery isn't currency here.

If that's too rich, house market takes five per cent — some teams run cheaper. Look around.

Ay, hijo, el puesto bien, mucha gente, mucho ruido. But fourteen? No, no — six P, like I said, and not one more. You are starting, cariño; keep your money for the packs of El Chato tonight. ¿Has comido ya? Take the card, cuídala.

¡Eh, amigo! Paco: ¡Qué ojo tienes! Nando: El mejor de la feria. Mira, para ti: el Cartel de Conciertos, cuatro primas. Una ganga, te lo juro por mi madre. Pero rápido, que la poli... digo, el taxi nos espera con el motor en marcha. ¿Sí o no?

"¡Hombre, qué generoso! Nando, did you hear him? But no, no, we're not thieves — eleven pesetas and she's yours, that's the honest word."

"Quick, quick, hermano, the van's running, we're gone in less than a minute — once we roll, we don't roll back. Eleven. Say sí!"

¡Ay, amigo, para el carro! Nando, ¿la Tienda de Discos? No, hombre — esa no la llevamos nosotros. El maletín está lleno de otras maravillas, pero esa carta no vive aquí. No te cobramos aire, que somos pícaros, no ladrones. ¡Otra vez será, amigo! Guarda tus primas para churros.
No. 84 P, and I'm being generous.
You move, I move. 13 P.

payload.name: Mercado Maravillas
payload.text: Mercado Maravillas: 0 % fee (El Rastro: 5 % + 1 P a card); post your bids and asks here and our broker crosses every pair that meets, each tick, at a price between both quotes. Sellers waiting here: MAL-02 from 3 P, LAV-01 from 6 P, LAV-03
Thirteen's a step. Not my step. Thirty-three, Mercado de la Paz. I don't move first.
Buenas. Mercado de San Ildefonso. Thirteen primas.
Una prima cada vez. Así no acabamos. Trece, La Rosaleda. Mi número no cambia.

¡Amigo, amigo! Paco here — Nando, show him the Cine Doré! A beauty, this one. For you, 73 P, because we like your face.

And listen — another crew cornered us by the door five minutes ago, offering us far more for it. We stalled them. But not for long, eh?
Buenas tardes, caballero. Lavapiés… en fin, no es Salamanca ni El Retiro. El Teatro Valle-Inclán, una uncommon corriente. Le ofrezco 16 P, y me parece un precio muy cortés por mi parte.

¡Ay, amigo, qué duro eres! Paco: Ocho, dice. Nando: ¡Nos rompe el corazón! Pero mira, por simpatía: el Cartel de Conciertos, cuatro primas. Mismo precio, mismo cariño, mismo taxi esperando. Mi hermano ya está cerrando la maleta. ¿Cuatro y te lo llevas, o nos vamos? ¡Venga, dime que sí!

"¡Catorce! Paco, he keeps counting backwards—" "—like a man walking home from a wedding." Amigo, we already said our number and we stand on it: cinco P, Huevos Rotos, in your hands, done. "Five, and our mother sleeps tonight." Cinco, sí? Say sí and we vanish.

"¡Otra vez más generoso que nosotros! Nando, this man's heart is bigger than the van."

"Eleven, amigo, eleven — we said it and we don't move, not up, not down. Paco's word is Paco's word."

"Take her, the engine's running. Eleven. ¡Dilo, sí!"

Ay, cariño, qué cabezota eres — ¡pero qué bien me caes! Twelve, no. Six P, the same as always, and I am happy with that. Guarda ese dinero for El Chato tonight, hijo. Take the Huevos Rotos, cuídala, and come Sunday with your duplicates. ¿Has comido algo?

payload.name: 🔥 MAD RUSH · 0% · LIVE NOW
payload.text: Market Test soon — MAD RUSH (v24) is 0%, 0 P per card, book open NOW. Post the card you need or a spare; we cross every tick. El Rastro takes 5% + 1 P per card.

Look, 6 P. My grandchildren would pay more! Look, cariño, I can't go lower. This is my last offer. El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 5 P. Last offer, amigo! Then we are gone, eh? Quick, quick, we leave in one minute!
You move, I move. 13 P.
One P. That's your big move? Thirteen. Same as before. I move when you move.
You moved six. I move one. Thirty-two, Mercado de la Paz. That's me off thirty-three. Your turn.
Buenas tardes. You arrive at a good moment — I am seeking "Vermut del Domingo" for my Salamanca album. I offer sixteen pesetas, a fair sum. Shall we deal, señor?
Sixty-five. Bien. Fiesta de San Cayetano, seventy-seven. Last one, chaval. You say no, I pack up and we both go home.

¡Dos! Nando, he jokes — he has the face of a collector, not a comedian! Look, amigo, we cut deep: 63 P, the Cine Doré is yours. Paco says we're mad, I say we're generous. That crew by the door is still waiting, eh? Decide fast, tell your friends after. ¡Vámonos!
You again. Fiesta de San Cayetano. Ninety-seven. Real card, no copies. Abuela sent you, so I'm being polite.
You keep bidding against yourself. Admirable. Thirteen primas, same as before.
La Latina, señor — charming, but not my album. Twenty-four is a figure for dreamers. Sixteen pesetas is what the card is worth, and what I pay. Shall we conclude like gentlemen?

Buenas tardes. A pleasure — though fifty-one is a figure for dreamers, not collectors. The Tienda de Discos is charming, yes, but hardly scarce. I offer sixteen. And do ask Carmen at El Rastro about the golden chulapa.

¡Tres! Nando, cover your ears — this man wants to break our hearts in Spanish! Bueno, bueno... 57 P. Paco is weeping behind the suitcase, truly. That is the Cine Doré, amigo, and that crew by the door is getting impatient. Say sí, and we both walk away smiling. ¡Rápido!
You moved one. I already moved one. Thirty-two stands, Mercado de la Paz. Cash is cash — but it isn't a discount. Your turn, amigo.
Caballero, por favor. No regateo contra mí misma: siguen siendo 16 P, ni un peso más. Lavapiés no me emociona. Si algún día me trae Salamanca o El Retiro, hablaremos con otro entusiasmo.

¡Siete! Paco: ¡Este hombre nos mata! Nando: ¡Pero qué arte tiene! Escucha: el Cartel de Conciertos, cuatro primas. Ni una más, ni una menos, mismo cariño de siempre. ¡Rápido, rápido, que nos vamos en un minuto! Mi hermano ya tiene un pie en la calle. ¿Cuatro? ¡Dime que sí, amigo!
Catorce. Movió una, muevo una. La Rosaleda, 14 P. Así se hace, poquito a poco.
You move, I move. 15 P.
You move, I move. 13 P.
Crisp corners are a pleasure, señor, but they do not change the print run. Forty-four remains a dream. My figure is sixteen — fair, and I do not haggle with myself. Think it over calmly.

Generous, señor? Generosity would be accepting a fair price without theatre. Twenty-one is a number from your imagination, not from the market. Sixteen pesetas, as I said, and as I shall continue to say. ¿Cerramos?

¡Cuatro! Nando, hold me — my heart! Escucha, amigo: 52 P. That is the last word, the final one, no more dancing. Say sí now or Paco shuts the suitcase, we sell to the crew by the door, and we walk. Fifty-two, or adiós. ¡Decide!

Hola, cariño! Come, sit a little, the sun is strong. Have you eaten? Look here — Mercado de la Cebada, a pretty one, my favourite stall card. For you, five P. My little Mateo started his album with that very one.

¡Amigo, amigo, ven aquí! Paco, abre la maleta —

— ya está abierta, hermano. Mira esto: Caña en la Cava Baja, rarísima, la última que nos queda. Un primo nuestro lloró cuando la vendimos.

Para ti, porque tienes buena cara: cuatro. Cuatro y te la llevas ahora mismo.
Four from you, two from me. Thirty, Mercado de la Paz. Your turn, amigo.
One P at a time, eh. Fine. Fourteen. I matched you. Next move is yours, and make it a real one.

payload.name: Gacela · 0% fee
payload.text: Gacela (v05) reads every trade in Madrid so yours closes first. Our broker crosses every tick at the fair midpoint, 0% fee and 0 P per card for both sides. List your spares and want-to-buy bids (give cash, want {"cards": ["LAV-03"]}) with a
No. 14 P, and I'm being generous.
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 4 P.
Oh, oh... 5 P, and only because you have a kind face.
Still falling on your own. Thirteen primas.
One from you, one from me. Twenty-nine, Mercado de la Paz. Morning crowd doesn't worry me. Your turn.
You moved nine. I move one. Ninety-six. That's how it works, amigo.
Dieciséis. La Rosaleda, 16 P. Última. Si dice que no, me levanto y asunto cerrado.
Thirty-four is still a shoebox price dressed up, señor. I will stretch to seventeen — a courtesy, not a negotiation. Your card would rest well in Salamanca. Decide calmly; I shall not move again.
Nineteen is not meeting, señor — it is you walking in place. I have known this card's print run since before you were born. Sixteen pesetas, firm and final. Take it, and we part as gentlemen.
Caballero, bajar un peso cada vez no es negociar, es hacerme perder la tarde. Mi palabra no cambia: 16 P por el Teatro Valle-Inclán. Acéptelos, o guarde su Lavapiés con mi bendición.

payload.name: Puesto de Team 17
payload.text: LAT-01 Caña en la Cava Baja: venta a 6 P y compra a 5 P en otros puestos, a 1 P de distancia. Aquí, sin comisión, quien opera desde El Rastro se ahorra su comisión. / LAT-01 Caña en la Cava Baja: ask 6 P, bid 5 P on other venues, 1 P apart.
No. 14 P, and I'm being generous.
I think 18 P is more appropriate.
Seventeen, then. A peseta for your persistence, señor — consider it a gift to your pride. The card is mine, and the matter is closed. Un placer. My album thanks you, even if my purse grumbles.
Thirteen from you. Two from me. Noventa y cuatro. Keep walking my way, we finish today.

¡Eh, amigo, amigo! Come, come — Paco saw you first, so you get the good one. Café de Madrugada, fresh from the case, still warm —

— still warm, yes! Four P and it's yours. Four! Nando's hand is shaking, he hates this price. Quick, before the crowd comes.

Ay, hija, no, no — such numbers! For you it stays five P, nothing more. I am not here to empty your purse, I am here to start your album. Take it at five, and come tomorrow anyway — I will have café and a little story waiting.

¡Hermano, escucha! Es la última en todo Madrid, te lo juro por mi madre. No hay otra, ni en Chamberí ni en Lavapiés. Nando ya está cerrando la maleta, tenemos un tren...

Cuatro. Cuatro y es tuya ahora mismo, amigo. Después me lo agradeces.
One from you, one from me. Twenty-eight, Mercado de la Paz. Last one, amigo. You say no, I pack the card and we're done.
